files.h:
Proves a goal-only run can start, and that the seed never puts words in the owner's mouth.

WHY THIS GATE EXISTS
The bug it guards was invisible for eleven days: routines and WhatsApp approvals queued runs
whose instruction lived only in `run.goal`, the runner rebuilt the conversation from a log
containing nothing but `run.status` bookkeeping, found zero messages, and dead-lettered the
run with `attempts: 0`. Nothing threw, nothing alerted, and the tenant's daily marketing
simply never happened. A fix for that cannot be left to inspection.

The failure modes worth pinning:
  - a goal-bearing run does not get seeded (the original bug)
  - a seed is written in a shape the event log cannot replay (silent on resume)
  - a run that ALREADY has a conversation gets a fabricated user turn appended, which would
    corrupt a real transcript and duplicate what the owner actually said
  - a run with no goal gets seeded with an empty turn, which the model would read as the
    owner saying nothing and then act on

Proves the scraping capability behaves itself — with NO network, NO R2 and NO
real clock.

The rules this file pins, and why each one is here rather than in a live run:

 - `robots.txt` parsing: `Disallow` honoured, `Allow` beating a broader

   asserted to have never been called — a warning-and-proceed would pass a
   "returned no rows" test, so this asserts the request instead);

   hostname resolving to a private address, and `file:`/`data:` URLs;
 - one in-flight request per host, a token bucket that actually waits, and a

 - the same URL twice inside the TTL is ONE page request, ONE R2 PUT and ONE

An approval card must survive the discovery proxy.

THE BUG
The model reaches most tools through `call_tool`, which wraps the real result:
`{ ok, tool, result }`. Every renderer looked for `output.artifact` at the TOP
level, so for any proxied tool:

  - the approval card was never drawn. `nobogent_whatsapp_send_template` and

    ALWAYS proxied — their card could never appear at all;
  - a question asked through the proxy never reached the question panel;
  - image / audio / video artefacts from proxied tools rendered as a bare row.

With no card there is no tap, and the gate only unlocks an action whose approval
row says `approved` — so the action was not merely hidden, it was impossible.

Does an agent-placed call actually get a voice?

The bug this covers was the worst kind: calls connected, billed and were silent. Vobiz reported 12 s and 9 s of
a real answered call, and the caller heard nothing. The cause was not the dialler — it was WHICH PIPELINE answered.
The default answer route points at the Gemini Live bridge, which accepts the media socket, completes its setup
handshake, and then emits zero audio frames; the Gemini TTS-Flash bridge, on a separate deployment, is the one the
demo page uses successfully.

So this asserts three things:
  1. the TTS-Flash bridge is up and its answer webhook returns a real <Stream> (not a Hangup),
  2. the agent's dispatcher DIALS that pipeline, with a voice named, and does not fall back to the Live route,
  3. the option actually survives the hop from the tool into the telephony helper — it did not, which is exactly
     why the first fix attempt looked right and behaved identically.

Point 2 and 3 are read from source with comments stripped, because a comment explaining a fix must never be
enough to satisfy the test for that fix.

WHAT THIS PINS
The feature is inheritance, so the tests are about inheritance:

  1. THE SCENARIO IS DERIVED FROM THE LEAD, in a fixed order. A booking beats everything, an
     untouched lead beats silence, and only elapsed time (14 days) makes a win-back.
  2. AN OVERRIDE WINS, AND ONLY WHAT IT SETS. A scenario that sets a voice but no script keeps the
     account's script, and the source of each part is reported so the UI and the agent can both say
     where the words came from.
  3. NOTHING SET MEANS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO TODAY. An account that never opens this feature must get
     exactly the script it got before, from exactly the same layer.
  4. THE STORED JSON CANNOT PRODUCE A SCRIPTLESS CALL. Unrecognised keys, wrong types and broken
     JSON all degrade to "inherit", never to an empty script.
  5. THE PLACEHOLDERS ARE FILLED, from the same renderer the default path uses.

  npm run verify:voice-scenarios

Can the agent actually see the WhatsApp templates it is told to use?

The defect this covers was found by running a real flow: the tool listed templates from the
`whatsapp_templates` table, which is EMPTY for an account that never imported into it, so a business with 35
APPROVED templates on its WABA was told "there are none" — and "send a test template" was impossible. Nothing
errored; the agent was simply told the opposite of the truth, which is the worst shape of bug.

So this asserts the fix at the level that matters: the list comes from Meta, it is the same list Meta will accept
for sending, it carries the variable count a caller needs, and an account with no WhatsApp connection gets a
clear reason instead of a cheerful empty list.

  npx esbuild scripts/verify-whatsapp-templates.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --packages=external \

TOOLCHAIN PROBE — **not** the P3 deliverable. Read this before trusting a frame.

This harness exists to prove one thing: that the emitted project compiles,
validates and renders, and that the beat timings actually drive picture and type.
Every pixel of input is a STAND-IN:

  - the "voice" is one ffmpeg tone burst per beat, not TTS. No vendor is called
    and no credit is spent, so nothing here tests voice, pricing or R2;
  - the plates are borrowed 1080x1920 footage from the delivered reference film
    (`--footage`), copied into the slots a generated clip would fill. Earlier
    revisions of this harness used flat gradient / colour-bar plates instead; in
    both cases the plate is a placeholder, never deliverable footage;
  - the logo is a solid cream PNG, so the end card's wordmark area is blank.

A film delivered by the `video` skill has real voiceover from the registry's voice
model, plates that are either the client's own footage or generated motion, and a
real brand asset. This file is the harness that proves the plumbing, not a film —
do not ship its output to a client.

files.h:
Standalone durable-run worker.

The cron route is one way to advance the queue (serverless, every minute).
This is the other: an always-on process that polls the queue continuously, for
hosts where a long-lived process is allowed (a container, a VM, E2B, or your
laptop). Same claim/lease/checkpoint semantics — the queue does not care who
drains it, and N of these can run side by side.

  npm run worker

Env:
  WORKER_POLL_MS        idle poll interval          (default 2000)
  WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS  lease length                (default 300)
  WORKER_MAX_PER_USER   concurrent runs per user    (default 2)
  WORKER_MAX_TOTAL      concurrent runs overall     (default 8)
  WORKER_SLICE_BUDGET_MS  per-slice wall clock      (default 1500000)
  WORKER_SLICE_MAX_STEPS  per-slice step cap        (default 30)

SIGINT/SIGTERM stop it cleanly: it finishes the slice in flight (so the
checkpoint is written and the lease released) and exits.

files.h:
Central resolution of the public app URL and voice-bridge URL.

Why this exists
---------------
These values are pasted into the Vercel dashboard by hand, and a pasted
value can silently carry invisible characters - most often a UTF-8 BOM
(U+FEFF) when the string is copied out of a file, but also zero-width
spaces or a stray pair of quotes.

Those characters are invisible in the dashboard but they are *truthy*, so
the usual `process.env.X || 'https://fallback'` keeps them and every URL
built from the value is no longer an absolute URL:

  answer_url = "\uFEFFhttps://app.nobogent.com/api/voice/vobiz/xml?..."

Vobiz then rejects the call with `answer_url parameter is not valid`, the
call is never placed, and the only user-visible symptom is
"AI calling doesn't work" - no exception, no call record, nothing to grep.
The same corruption also poisons status/recording callbacks and the
telephony WebSocket stream URL.

Resolution therefore strips invisible characters, surrounding quotes,
whitespace and trailing slashes, and falls back to the known-good value
when nothing usable survives.

files.h:
Follow-up activity accounting — the single source of truth for "how many follow-ups
did each rep log, and when".

WHY THIS MODULE EXISTS
----------------------
The Analytics page used to answer that question three different ways:

  • Followup Board   → every lead_history row whose text mentioned "call"/"followup"
  • Action Report    → the same rows, but re-dated from whatever date happened to
                       appear in the description, then de-duplicated
  • Team matrix      → the raw row count again

The Action Report's re-dating was the expensive bug. `parseActionDate()` grabbed the
first date-looking token anywhere in the description, and follow-ups written by the
offline fallback end with "Next Action: Call on 21/10/2026, 15:40:00". So the *next
action* date was read as the *time the action happened*: any follow-up whose agent
typed a past next-action date silently vanished from today's numbers. A lead filed as
"Next Action: Call on 11/17/2026" was read as month 17 → JS rolled it into May 2027.
That is how a rep who logged 9 follow-ups was told he logged 7.

files.h:
Lead history & pending-action visibility.

Product rule (this is the whole reason this module exists):

  1. Lead history is **never deleted**. Not on transfer, not ever.
  2. When a lead is transferred, the sender may choose to hide the previous
     history from the receiving teammate. That is a *visibility cutoff*, not a
     deletion: a `history_visible_from` timestamp is stamped on the lead and
     anything older than it is hidden **from non-admin viewers only**.
  3. Admins (`super_admin`, `agency`, `admin`) always see the complete
     history, including everything before the cutoff.
  4. The lead **source** (where the lead came from — Meta form, ad, campaign,
     CSV import, manual entry) is always visible to everyone, even when the
     rest of the history is hidden. An agent must always be able to see what
     the lead is and where it came from in order to work it.
  5. Pending / scheduled actions (next follow-up, booked time, next action
     notes) follow the same rule via `pending_actions_hidden`: hidden from the
     receiving teammate, always visible to admins, and
